title: Content Writing — Objective Assessment
instructions: Carefully read each question and select the most appropriate answer from options A-D. Each question carries equal marks. Multiple-choice questions are marked automatically when you submit.

questions.prompt: What does the rule “one post equals one idea” mean?
options: Every post should contain only one sentence.
Each post should focus on one main idea rather than several different ideas.
A writer should publish only one post per day.
Each post should use only one type of visual.

questions.prompt: Why is it important for a writer to understand their audience before creating content?
options: It allows the writer to use more complicated vocabulary.
It helps determine what information, language, and approach will be relevant.
It guarantees that everyone will agree with the content.
It allows the writer to avoid having a clear purpose.

questions.prompt: What is the primary difference between active voice and passive voice?
options: Active voice uses shorter words, while passive voice uses longer words.
In active voice, the subject performs the action; in passive voice, the subject receives the action.
Active voice is only used in fiction, while passive voice is used in nonfiction.
Active voice describes emotions, while passive voice describes physical actions.

questions.prompt: Which hashtag strategy does the second video recommend for Instagram captions?
options: Use all 30 hashtags Instagram allows on every post.
Avoid hashtags completely because they never help content get discovered.
Use long, general hashtags to attract the widest possible audience.
Use one or two relevant hashtags to target a specific audience.

questions.prompt: According to the video, what is the first step in creating an engaging LinkedIn post?
options: Adding an attractive image to the post.
Writing a catchy hook immediately.
Finding a unique, fresh, and interesting insight.
Adding hashtags to increase visibility.

questions.prompt: What can happen when content does not have a clear purpose?
options: The content may contain many words without actually accomplishing anything.
The audience will automatically understand the message.
The content becomes more persuasive.
The writer becomes more creative.

questions.prompt: Consider the sentence: "He was running down the street." Which revision follows the recommendation to reduce unnecessary "was + verb-ing" constructions?
options: He had been running down the street.
He was quickly running down the street.
He ran down the street.
He continued to be running down the street.

questions.prompt: According to the first video, why should social media writers aim to communicate their message in as few words as possible?
options: Longer posts are not allowed on social media platforms.
People often scroll or skim quickly, so concise writing helps capture their attention.
Short posts do not require correct grammar or spelling.
Short posts automatically receive more likes and comments.

questions.prompt: What are the three main roles of a good LinkedIn hook?
options: Entertain the reader, advertise a product, and include hashtags.
Trigger interest, make the topic clear, and help readers feel that the content is relevant to them.
Introduce the writer, explain their background, and summarize the conclusion.
Provide every detail, answer all questions, and end the discussion.

questions.prompt: Which question helps a writer determine the audience's existing level of knowledge?
options: What platform should I publish on?
How long should my article be?
What does my audience already know?
What font should I use?

questions.prompt: Why should writers avoid using overly complicated sentences too frequently?
options: Complicated sentences are always grammatically incorrect.
They prevent writers from including descriptive details.
They can slow down reading, obscure the main point, and distance readers from the action.
They make every piece of writing sound informal.

questions.prompt: According to the second video, why does it recommend beginning LinkedIn captions with an intriguing hook?
options: It encourages readers to click “see more” and continue reading.
It allows users to publish without writing a complete message.
It guarantees that every reader will follow the account.
It removes the need to include a call to action.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of a content purpose?
options: Increasing the number of words in an article.
Making the writer sound intelligent.
Educating the audience about a subject.
Using as many writing techniques as possible.

questions.prompt: According to the video, which of the following is a useful way to discover original insights for LinkedIn content?
options: Copying popular posts from successful creators.
Repeating the same ideas used by competitors.
Writing only about trending topics without considering personal experience.
Analyzing audience questions, documenting daily experiments, and reflecting on personal experiences.

questions.prompt: How can sentence length influence the pace and mood of a piece of writing?
options: Short sentences generally convey urgency and tension, while longer sentences can create a more reflective, thoughtful mood.
Longer sentences always make writing more exciting, while shorter sentences make it boring.
Sentence length has no effect on how readers experience a story.
Short sentences are appropriate only for dialogue, while longer sentences are appropriate only for descriptions.
